Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about his eyesight. He sits way too close to the TV when watching cartoons and also when reading books. I've tried to get him to move back a bit, but he says he can't see as well then.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes I call his name and he doesn't respond right away. It's like he's not hearing me or maybe just ignoring me? But if I go over to him and say it again، he'll usually answer. I don't know if it's his hearing or just him being a bit distracted.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are a worry for me because the dentist said the enamel is weak. We have to be super careful with sugary foods and make sure he brushes them really well to prevent cavities.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When he plays outside with friends， his breathing gets much faster than the other kids. Even when they're all running around together， my son seems to be panting more. I've mentioned it to his dad， but we haven't done anything about it yet.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Poor baby... he has low muscle tone. The physiotherapist is working with him to improve it. You can see it when he walks or tries to hold things; it's just a bit more effortful for him than for other kids his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Eating can be tricky sometimes. He's super fussy about food textures and won't eat certain things because of how they feel in his mouth. Like， mashed potatoes are okay but not if they're lumpy at all.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... his fingers are shorter than usual. We were told it's just something he was born with and doesn't affect anything else.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing when playing outside with friends, even when other kids are running around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets much faster than other kids when playing outside, suggesting potential cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is fussy about food textures and refuses to eat certain things due to how they feel in his mouth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has low muscle tone, which affects his ability to walk or hold things, requiring physical therapy to improve.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, with some children needing more support and others benefiting from specialist settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring support from family or friends.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and difficulty making himself understood, as well as palatal abnormalities and undescended testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A small number of children with KBG syndrome have had hip dysplasia, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and periodic palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring respiratory rate during exercise, considering physiotherapy and occupational therapy, managing low muscle tone, addressing palatal abnormalities, and managing undescended testes.

This completes the required clinical patient report.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in her heart, requiring regular check-ups to monitor it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties since birth, including difficulty swallowing certain textures and often gags on her food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to sit, stand, and walk compared to other kids as a baby, suggesting possible developmental delays, but the concern remains about potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay, behavioral differences, and speech delay.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods, and has trouble seeing the board in class.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have feeding difficulties and speech delay, which can be exacerbated by palatal abnormalities and other factors.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class and has difficulty swallowing certain textures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties and speech delay, which can be influenced by various factors such as palatal abnormalities and sensory issues.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity and has difficulty swallowing certain textures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding has been a challenge since birth for many with KBG syndrome, and some may require short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delay and feeding difficulties impact her educational performance, making her anxious about mealtime and hesitant to participate fully in lessons.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some needing support in mainstream settings and others possibly benefiting from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows signs of developmental delay, behavioral differences, and speech delay, which are concerning for parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, behavioral differences, and speech delay are common features in KBG syndrome, with some individuals experiencing more significant challenges than others.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which requires monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Various skeletal anomalies can be present in KBG syndrome, including asymmetric hip creases, asymmetric or painful gait, and tethered cord, which may require medical intervention.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology assessments are recommended.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve issues, treatment for palatal abnormalities, management of feeding difficulties, and consideration of neurodevelopmental therapies based on individual needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups to monitor a previously identified condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding aversion, making mealtime challenging and difficult to achieve a balanced diet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower coordination when moving, taking longer to master simple tasks like tying shoes or riding a bike, and sometimes tripping over her own feet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have more significant neurological concerns such as tethered cord, skeletal anomalies, or palatal abnormalities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and affect her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have feeding difficultyssuch as squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, and speech delay, which may be linked to their hearing concerns.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision), and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), which may affect her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, which makes dental health a concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties can make dental care challenging, and some individuals may require longer-term tube feeding.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower speech development and takes longer to master simple tasks, affecting her academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have varying levels of educational attainment, with some obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower development and coordination, impacting her overall physical and cognitive abilities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to various complications such as tethered cord, hip dysplasia, and asymmetric hip creases.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular heart check-ups to monitor a previously identified condition.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A
c) Additional recommendations: Consider a palate review, especially if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns, and refer for a cardiac review following diagnosis.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... my baby squints quite a bit, and it's really concerning because I worry it might affect his ability to learn and interact with others. I've tried to get him to wear glasses, but he doesn't like them very much.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Well... he does get frustrated when there's too much noise around him. Like in malls or at school. It's almost as if the sounds overwhelm him. But otherwise, his hearing seems fine.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Poor thing... his teeth break or chip so easily! It's like they're made of glass or something. We have to be super careful what he eats and make sure he brushes them just right.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... he gets tired more quickly than the other kids. Even after just playing for a little while. It worries me because I want him to be able to run around and have fun like everyone else.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has hypotonia... low muscle tone. The physiotherapist says it's why he has trouble with certain movements and balance. We're working on exercises to help strengthen his muscles.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Actually... yes. He has a feeding aversion. Certain foods just don't agree with him. And sometimes... well... let's just say mealtime can be challenging.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: There are these undescended testes... and how he moves is a bit different from his friends. Not in a bad way... just... unique. And the doctor did mention something about needing to monitor those testes further.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion and difficulty with certain foods, potentially impacting his vision and eyesight.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space and not responding immediately upon being called, suggesting possible neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned having trouble seeing the board at school, particularly when the teacher writes in small letters or from a distance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods like meat or crunchy vegetables, requiring modifications to mealtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental check-ups are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue during physical activities and requires rest frequently, affecting his ability to participate fully in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome may need additional support in mainstream education, with some benefiting from special schooling or having EHCP.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays developmental delays and lacks clarity in communication, making interaction with peers and adults challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can impact their daily life and interactions.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which may lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, which requires monitoring and treatment to prevent future complications.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences breathlessness and needs rest sooner when engaging in physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than other kids and requires rest sooner after physical activity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has struggled with bowel movements, experiencing constipation and discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and needs to take medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid in his ear, which may affect his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of his eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and requires careful brushing to prevent tooth decay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent cavities can be common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has required additional support in school, including EHCP, and may need assistance with certain tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support. 

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and lacks interest in certain activities, suggesting potential behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may display various levels of developmentally迟缓，从轻微到显著不等。

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), as well as hip dysplasia and tethered cord.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Subtle anomalies of the palate and undescended testes in boys are occasionally observed in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
The main recommendations for screening and treatments based on the provided consultation are:

a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5 (if not previously responded to).
c) Ophthalmology review.

f) Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
g) Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis.
h) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
i) Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty keeping up during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties and an aversion to certain foods, making mealtime a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures and struggles with physical activity, indicating possible neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and affect her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, and some have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental check-ups and has various dental concerns, including weak enamel and potential need for corrective procedures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to prevent complications and maintain oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with physical activity and learning, which may impact her educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, children with KBG syndrome have varying levels of success, with some acquiring mainstream qualifications and others needing additional support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and struggles with physical activity, affecting her overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may experience delays in reaching milestones such as walking, sitting, and using cutlery and zips, but there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with an increased incidence of skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia, tethered cord, and palatal abnormalities.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic reviews for heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for scoliosis, considering hormonal treatments if necessary, managing seizures, and addressing any palatal abnormalities or tethered cord issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Honestly, I'm worried about his eyesight. He complains that things look blurry sometimes, and it's hard to know if it's just a phase or something more serious. I've noticed he squints or rubs his eyes frequently.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... he seems to have trouble hearing certain sounds. Like, when we're watching TV, he'll ask us to turn it up because he can't hear it well. It's concerning because he should be able to pick up on conversations and shows easily at his age.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has become a challenge for him lately. Harder foods like apples or meat are difficult for him to manage. We've had to adjust his diet somewhat to softer foods to make mealtime less stressful.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physical activity... he just can't seem to keep up with the other kids. Even simple games like tag or running around leave him winded and tired quickly. It worries me that there might be an underlying issue we need to address.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: The tethered cord issue is something we're closely monitoring. The specialists have assured us they're on top of it, but it's still a concern for us as parents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Mealtime... it's often a struggle. He has days where eating is just really hard for him. The food either doesn't agree with him or he's just not interested. We try to keep a routine and offer a variety of foods to see what works best for him.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well... aside from what we've discussed, his movements are slightly different from his peers. And he was diagnosed with scoliosis. These are things we're working through with his therapists and doctors to ensure he gets the right support and care.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty keeping up with physical activities, leaving him winded and tired quickly, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has struggles with eating and mealtime, experiencing difficulty eating or being uninterested in food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences neurological issues, specifically tethered cord, which requires close monitoring and intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and affect his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint (strabismus), where the eyes do not look in the same direction, can occasionally be a feature, and treatment may include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty chewing harder foods like apples or meat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent tooth decay may be more common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with physical activities and difficulty keeping up with peers, affecting his overall educational performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome may need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream environments with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including palatal abnormalities and scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, children with KBG syndrome typically experience delays in reaching milestones such as rolling, sitting, walking, and using cutlery, zips, and buttons. However, there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia, where the hip joints are easily dislocated.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic examinations to monitor the tethered cord issue.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing heart conditions, addressing tethered cord issues, providing physiotherapy and occupational therapy to support movement and daily functions, ensuring adequate nutrition and preventing vitamin deficiencies, and considering speech therapy to address any communication difficulties.

This completes the required clinical patient report.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in her heart and requires regular check-ups every few months to monitor it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and has trouble eating certain foods due to texture aversions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences falls more often than other kids her age and has difficulty maintaining balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media and glue ear, requiring treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and palatal abnormalities, which may impact her vision and lead to squint (strabismus).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent cavities due to poor oral hygiene and weak enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to prevent complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school and may require accommodations to assist with learning challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits speech delay and palatal abnormalities, which may impact her development and communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delays and behavioral differences are commonly observed in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), which may affect her posture and mobility.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology evaluations.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve issues, treatment of otitis media and glue ear, management of palatal abnormalities, and consideration of speech therapy and physical therapy based on individual needs.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has myopia, which means he has trouble seeing things that are far away. We've gotten him glasses to help correct this, and it's made a big difference in his ability to see the board at school and watch TV without squinting.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He seems to have some difficulty hearing certain sounds or frequencies. It's not a profound hearing loss or anything, but there are definitely times when he doesn't pick up on everything being said, especially in noisy environments. We're considering having his hearing tested again to see if there's anything more going on.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Dental care has been a bit of an issue for him. He needs to go to the dentist more often than most kids his age because of some tooth decay and sensitivity issues. We're working on teaching him better oral hygiene habits to try and prevent more problems down the line.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, his heart rate can get pretty high when he's playing or running around. Not dangerously so, but enough that we notice it and the doctors are keeping an eye on it to make sure it doesn't develop into anything more serious.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He does seem to tire easily when he's physically active. Whether it's playing soccer or just running around in the park, he gets winded faster than his friends. We're not sure if it's related to his overall health or just his fitness level, but it's something we're watching.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Actually, yes. When he was a baby, feeding was a real challenge. He had trouble latching on and would often spit up. Luckily, that's mostly resolved itself as he got older, though we still deal with occasional constipation issues.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: One thing that's concerned us is his speech development. For his age, we expect him to be saying a lot more than he currently is. The specialists are looking into this, and we're doing exercises at home to encourage more talk.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit varying levels of delay, ranging from mild to severe, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as typical children and others showing more pronounced delay.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and there are instances of hip dysplasia and tethered cord, which require monitoring and intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies such as hip dysplasia and tethered cord can affect movement and posture, leading to unique gait or functional limitations.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic assessments for palatal abnormalities.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are weak and prone to breaking or chipping, requiring careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed extra help in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others staying in mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and has difficulty making certain movements and gestures.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, which can be painful and take a long time to resolve.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are not very frequent but do happen. He needs to be very vigilant and ensure he's taking his medication as prescribed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be difficult to treat in some cases.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to turn the volume of the TV very high, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when looking at things, particularly when they're close up, indicating potential vision issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and breaks or chips easily, requiring careful brushing and monitoring by a dentist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and need for frequent dental visits are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing himself clearly and getting his thoughts across, leading to frustration and challenges in communicating effectively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome may need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream environments with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with clarity when trying to talk, getting his words mixed up and experiencing difficulty expressing himself clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, individuals with KBG syndrome may experience delays in reaching certain milestones, but there is a wide range of eventual ability, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with various skeletal anomalies, including delayed fontanelle closure and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of septal defect, treatment of seizures, management of constipation, and consideration of orthopedic interventions based on clinical findings.

Parent: Her teeth have weak enamel. We have to ensure she brushes them carefully and regularly visits the dentist for check-ups to prevent any further issues. The dentist has also recommended a special toothpaste to help strengthen her teeth.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain‚ nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Developmentally‚ she has been slower to reach certain milestones‚ such as walking or sitting unassisted. While she eventually achieves these milestones‚ it takes her longer than her peers. We work closely with physical therapists to support her development.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned conditions‚ our child struggles with speech clarity. She finds it hard to express herself clearly‚ which can be frustrating for her. Additionally‚ she has a delayed fontanelle closure‚ where her soft palate doesn't move properly during speech‚ affecting her pronunciation. These are areas we're working on with speech therapists.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems such as constipation and occasional diarrhea. Managing her diet and ensuring she stays hydrated helps alleviate these issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate can affect speech development and feeding, requiring specialist review in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been slower to reach developmental milestones such as walking or sitting unassisted, but eventually achieves them. Physical therapy supports her development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty in noisy environments, suggesting a potential issue with her sense of hearing or balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her vision at close range and makes reading and focusing more difficult.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer than peers to achieve developmental milestones and requires support in school through physical therapy and speech therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education can vary greatly depending on the individual, but many children with KBG syndrome need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, and while some children acquire mobility and other skills around the same age as "typical" children, others show more obvious delay.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study showed that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, regular hearing reviews, and periodic heart check-ups.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring heart health, strengthening teeth with special toothpaste, managing bowel problems through dietary adjustments, and addressing speech clarity through therapy.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition characterized by faster-than-normal heartbeats when active, requiring monitoring but not immediate concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some needing surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty eating certain foods and often feels full quickly, making meal times stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding and others needing monitoring for potential palatal abnormalities or anomalies of the roof of the mouth.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed with a plan.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be challenging but manageable with medication and monitoring.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss and require periodic checks and treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, requiring glasses for clearer vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, with regular eye checks and corrective lenses being necessary.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental visits due to cavities and weak enamel, with encouragement for better brushing habits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues like cavities and weak enamel are common, necessitating regular check-ups and preventive measures.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows variability in academic performance, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children finishing mainstream education and others benefiting from specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears generally behind peers in development, adding to existing challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delays are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, with unique features such as speech delay, palatal abnormalities, and skeletal anomalies impacting overall development.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), which may impact movement and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with various skeletal anomalies, including delayed fontanelle closure, hip dysplasia, and tethered cord, which can influence mobility, posture, and overall physical development.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic reviews for palatal abnormalities or anomalies of the roof of the mouth.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing heart conditions, treating seizures, correcting feeding difficulties, and addressing any additional medical concerns as they arise.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges with bowel movements, getting constipated easily if dietary intake is insufficient.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, characterized by weak muscles, and shorter fingers than usual.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty focusing on distant objects, suggesting possible visual clarity issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring more support.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, with some children showing significant delay and others demonstrating more typical development.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may contribute to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology assessments are recommended.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring for septal defects, consideration of surgery if necessary, management of hypotonia, and addressing feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities as they arise.

Parent: She complains that things look blurry sometimes. We've taken her to get her eyes checked, and we're waiting to see if she needs glasses.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she doesn't respond when we call her name. It's like she doesn't hear us, but we're not sure if it's a hearing problem or just her not paying attention.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem to break or chip really easily. We have to be super careful with what she eats and make sure she brushes them regularly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When she plays or runs around, her breathing gets faster than we'd expect. The doctor said it might be something to monitor, but so far it hasn't caused any big issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: She has epilepsy. We work closely with her doctors to manage it and make sure she takes her medication as prescribed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a challenge for her. Some foods she just can't tolerate well, and it affects her bowel movements.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: She moves a bit differently compared to her peers. Also, there are some concerns about palatal abnormalities that the specialists are looking into.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when playing or running around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing or running around, suggesting potential cardiac issues that may need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced feeding challenges and some foods she cannot tolerate well, affecting her bowel movements.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves a bit differently compared to her peers, indicating possible neurological or muscular development issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be difficult to treat, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and asymmetric gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has complained of blurred vision, suggesting potential hearing or ear-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurred vision and squints, which may indicate astigmatism or other vision-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental visits due to tooth sensitivity and potential cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular check-ups are essential to prevent complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school, requiring accommodations and interventions tailored to her needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some achieving mainstream qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including palatal abnormalities that are being investigated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as "typical" children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may contribute to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can lead to various complications such as sacral dimple and abnormal gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiovascular assessments.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring respiratory rate during physical activity, managing seizure episodes, treating palatal abnormalities, and considering orthopedic intervention based on specific findings.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected during physical activity, which has been a concern for a while.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing becomes faster than what is expected for a child of her age during physical activity, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion to certain foods, making meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, requiring management from a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media and glue ear, leading to recurrent ear infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and necessitate treatment with antibiotics or drainage tubes.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental visits due to various issues, including weak enamel and potential tooth decay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. Levels of employment and the nature of employment varies but many do undertake some form of paid employment.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and has difficulty with certain tasks, such as playing with toys and using cutlery, zips and buttons.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as "typical" children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Various skeletal anomalies can be present in individuals with KBG syndrome, including delayed fontanelle closure, hip dysplasia, and tethered cord.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, regular hearing reviews to age 5, and periodic ophthalmology reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing seizure episodes, treating otitis media and glue ear, correcting palatal abnormalities, and addressing skeletal anomalies as they are identified.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences mealtime struggles, being picky about food and having trouble eating sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, characterized by stiff muscles, affecting her movement and balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid buildup in the ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasal grommet insertion to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia (nearsightedness), hypermetropia (far-sightedness), and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups and has weak enamel, making her prone to cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to prevent tooth decay and maintain overall oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support. 

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including hypotonia and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which can impact their daily lives.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, eyesight (ophthalmology) review, and consideration for cardiac and hormonal screenings based on individual clinical findings.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve abnormalities, treatment of hypotonia, management of palatal abnormalities, correction of tethered cord, management of hip dysplasia, and consideration of speech therapy and physical therapy as needed.
